I suspect the crash has more to do with the ignore on the @foo.setter line.

Can you use @abstractproperty? It exists in abc.py.

I think there's two (possibly related) bugs:
- You get `Function is missing a type annotation` despite not missing any type annotations.
- With the `# type: ignore`, mypy crashes. This crash happens in cache serialization. There's another related bug: `--pdb` doesn't work for crashes in serialization. The function it's crashing on serializing is the `setter` method.

As for the correct way to annotate this, from the code it looks like mypy expects you to annotate the getter, not the setter, with `@abstractmethod`. It also supports `@abstractproperty`, but that is deprecated.

issue.title: fix crash when serializing a type-ignored property setter
issue.body: This fixes two issues from #3491: a crash in serialization and an incorrect error "Function is missing a type annotation for one or more arguments". Both had the same root cause; we were skipping semantic analysis for the function body if mypy was unhappy with the property.setter decorator.

body: I fixed the crash in #3493, but I was unable to reproduce the bug with the `Function is missing a type annotation` message.
That error appears when you add `--disallow-untyped-defs`.
@gvanrossum I can use `@abstractproperty` for my use case and it does not exhibit the same issue with `mypy`. I'll use that for the time being.
OK, but we still need to figure out the reason for the spurious "Function is missing a type annotation" error.
Turns out my PR also fixes that. Mypy was complaining about `self` not having an annotation, probably because it skipped semantic analysis on the method.
